ip_top_stories.title: Round Hill Sues Suno, Anthropic — Illegally Scraped Music Isn't Fair Use
ip_top_stories.summary: Music rights company Round Hill has filed suit against AI companies Suno and Anthropic, arguing that using copyrighted music without authorisation to train AI models does not constitute fair use. The case adds to a growing body of music industry litigation targeting AI developers over training data practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Meta wins dismissal of AI training copyright suit, but amendment permitted
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has dismissed a copyright infringement lawsuit against Meta over its use of copyrighted works to train AI, though the plaintiffs have been granted permission to amend their complaint and refile. The case remains a closely watched test of whether AI training on protected content constitutes infringement.

ip_top_stories.title: WikiHow sues OpenAI for copyright infringement over AI training
ip_top_stories.summary: WikiHow has filed a copyright infringement lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that its content was used without permission to train AI models. The case joins a growing number of publisher-led actions challenging AI companies over training data sourcing.

ip_top_stories.title: Who's suing AI and who's signing latest: Editorial Perfil sues OpenAI, News Corp vs Brave
ip_top_stories.summary: A roundup of the latest AI copyright litigation and licensing developments includes Argentine publisher Editorial Perfil filing suit against OpenAI, and News Corp pursuing action against browser company Brave over AI-related content use. The piece charts the expanding landscape of both legal disputes and licensing agreements between media companies and AI developers.

ip_top_stories.title: Singapore seeks consultation on intellectual property regime's response to AI
ip_top_stories.summary: The Singapore government has launched a public consultation on how its intellectual property framework should respond to the rise of AI, including whether copyrighted works may be used for AI training. The consultation reflects growing regulatory pressure across Asia-Pacific to clarify AI and copyright rules.

ip_further_links.title: South Korea copyright collective rescinds new rules on AI-assisted music works
ip_further_links.summary: South Korea's music copyright collective KOMCA has withdrawn newly introduced standards for registering AI-assisted music works, stating it will consult further with the National Assembly and government before proceeding.

ip_further_links.title: A Hungarian local media legal battle against Google could shape the future of AI in Europe
ip_further_links.summary: A Hungarian media copyright case against Google is being watched closely as a potential precedent for how AI and copyright law will develop across Europe.

ip_further_links.title: If your art trained the AI, MIT says you may never be able to prove it
ip_further_links.summary: MIT researchers have found that artists and rights holders may face fundamental evidentiary barriers to proving their work was used in AI training datasets, complicating potential copyright claims.

ip_further_links.title: Twitch Streamer Sues Amazon Over AI Training, Claims Creator Content Used Without Consent
ip_further_links.summary: A Twitch streamer has filed a lawsuit against Amazon alleging their creative content was used without consent to train AI systems, expanding AI training copyright disputes into the creator economy.

ip_further_links.title: Vietnam tightens AI rules in amended publishing law
ip_further_links.summary: Vietnam has introduced stricter AI regulations through amendments to its publishing law, adding to a growing body of Asia-Pacific legislative responses to AI and intellectual property concerns.

ip_further_links.title: From Napster to Sampling to AI: Copyright Law's Role as the Sheriff to Emerging Technology
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis traces how copyright law has historically responded to disruptive technologies — from Napster to digital sampling — and what this history suggests for how courts and legislators may approach AI.

ip_further_links.title: The future of information: How should copyright law respond to Artificial Intelligence?
ip_further_links.summary: A broad examination of the legal and policy questions surrounding AI and copyright, considering what legislative and judicial reforms may be needed to address the challenges posed by AI-generated and AI-trained content.

ip_further_links.title: Code of Principles for AI: Can This Really Protect Intellectual Property?
ip_further_links.summary: An assessment of whether voluntary codes of principles for AI development can offer meaningful protection for intellectual property rights, or whether binding legislative intervention is required.

ip_further_links.title: MU Supports Creators Emergency Summit to Protect Creative Livelihoods Against AI
ip_further_links.summary: The Musicians' Union has announced its support for a Creators Emergency Summit aimed at protecting the livelihoods of creative professionals threatened by the rapid expansion of AI-generated content.

ip_further_links.title: AI Micro-Dramas Reshape the CP Economy: Virtual Characters Rack Up 5 Billion Views as Monetization and Copyright Risks Collide
ip_further_links.summary: AI-generated micro-drama content featuring virtual characters is accumulating billions of views online, raising novel copyright and monetisation questions as the boundary between human and AI-created content blurs.
